newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch prime minister urges action on world hunger.
newsitem.headline: Dutch prime minister urges action on world hunger.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on Tuesday signalled that he would use his country's presidency of the European Union to highlight the world's food problem, a crisis he called one of the greatest challenges for decades ahead.

In a speech to the University of Wageningen, Kok said he would launch a "passionate plea" for targeted and powerful cooperation at the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organisation's (FAO) World Food Summit in Rome in November.

"As a European politician I see it as a necessity that the European Union, at...the first ministerial conference of the WTO (World Trade Organisation) in December, at which the results of the World Food Summit will be discussed, should speak with one voice," he said.
The Dutch government will assume the rotating presidency of the European Union in January 1997 and Kok said the bloc's agricultural policy would form a key part of the discussion.

"The future of the common agricultural policy will therefore be the subject of discussion in the years ahead, partly in view of the imminent accession of countries from central and eastern Europe to the European Union," he said of a debate which is to begin in the spring under the Dutch presidency of the EU.
There were currently around 800 million undernourished people in the world and in 35 years' time the world would need between 75 and 100 percent more food than now.
He described international efforts to combat hunger, particularly those by the United Nations, as inadequate.

"It is sometimes painful to see how international coordination, partly because of internal competition between different UN organisations, so often falls short of what is needed," he added. REUTER 031258 GMT sep 96
